title: Microsoft 365 admin center: data quality report for people profile data
summary: The roadmap facts, service entry path and product-level licensing are supported. Two descriptive statements need narrowing: Microsoft does not explicitly establish that the report is read-only, and describes fragmented attributes as difficult, not impossible, to use for segmentation. All four Learn pages flagged by the pre-check opened successfully.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service is introducing a report assessing the completeness and health of people data.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Services is introducing a new data quality report that helps administrators assess the coverage and health of people data used across Microsoft 365 experiences.

claims.claim: The people data supports People Card, Org Explorer, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Cowork.
claims.quote: High-quality people data enables users to more effectively discover and learn about colleagues through experiences such as the People Card, Org Explorer, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Microsoft 365 Cowork.

claims.claim: Learn describes measurement of manager hierarchy health and user attribute health.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service measures the quality of two kinds of data:
1. The health of the manager hierarchy
2. The health of each user attribute

claims.claim: Hierarchy completeness is the percentage of employees with a complete, resolved manager chain.
claims.quote: Hierarchy completeness is the percentage of employees with a complete, resolved manager chain, or people who can be traced all the way up through valid manager relationships.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Missing manager is one of the hierarchy issue categories.
claims.quote: Missing manager | The person has no manager value at all.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An unresolved manager is a manager value that does not resolve to a person in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Unresolved manager | A manager value exists, but it doesn't resolve to a person in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Reporting loops are a hierarchy issue category.
claims.quote: Reporting loop | Two or more people report to each other in a cycle, so the chain never reaches the top.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The documented hierarchy measures include the number of separate hierarchy trees.
claims.quote: Tree count — the number of separate hierarchy trees.

claims.claim: The documented hierarchy measures include the share of employees in the largest tree.
claims.quote: Share of employees in the largest tree — what fraction of your people the main hierarchy contains.

claims.where: What's changing; Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Attribute coverage is the percentage of people with a value, including examples such as job title coverage.
claims.quote: Coverage is the percentage of people for whom an attribute has a value. A job title attribute with 89 percent coverage means 89 out of every 100 people in the measured population have a job title.

claims.claim: Unique values measures the number of distinct values an attribute holds.
claims.quote: Unique values, sometimes called "cardinality," is the number of distinct values an attribute holds.

claims.claim: An attribute with one value for everyone is not useful for segmentation.
claims.quote: When an attribute has only one distinct value, it's not useful for segmentation, because every person has the same value.

claims.claim: Attributes with too many distinct values cannot be used to group people.
claims.quote: Searched: "Organizational Data Service" "data quality" automatic remediation unique values segmentation. Read data-quality-metrics, Fragmented attributes: it says difficult to use for segmentation, not impossible to group.
claims.fix: Replace 'so many values that they cannot be used to group people' with 'so many values that they become difficult to use for segmentation', matching https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/org-data-service/manage/data-quality-metrics.

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly identify its metrics page as documentation of this newly announced admin-center report.
claims.quote: Searched: "data quality report" "People Administrator" "AI Administrator" Microsoft 365 access location. Read data-quality-metrics, get-started and organizational-data; none explicitly ties the metrics page to roadmap item 568937.

claims.claim: Learn says a quality report tells administrators what is wrong, not where to correct it.
claims.quote: A quality report tells you what's wrong, not where to correct it.

claims.claim: The quality report does not identify which source supplied a particular value.
claims.quote: A data quality report doesn't identify which source supplied any particular value.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Corrections generally belong in the authoritative source supplying the attribute and should involve the people-data pipeline owner.
claims.quote: Corrections generally belong in the authoritative source that supplies the attribute. The first step, therefore, is to talk to the team that owns your people-data pipeline rather than making an edit yourself.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot uses the manager hierarchy to determine who belongs to my team or my organization.
claims.quote: When someone asks Microsoft 365 Copilot about "my team" or "my organization," the agent uses the manager hierarchy to determine who to include.

claims.claim: Org Explorer uses the manager hierarchy to show reporting structure.
claims.quote: When Org Explorer shows where a person sits in their reporting structure, it's drawing the manager hierarchy.

claims.claim: A broken senior leader manager link can remove a whole branch from the organization-wide tree.
claims.quote: When a senior leader's manager link is broken, everyone who reports up through that leader falls out of the org-wide tree. A single bad value can create a missing branch representing hundreds or thousands of people.

claims.claim: The report's default state and what happens on arrival are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365" "data quality report" "enable" "default". Read roadmap record, data-quality-metrics, get-started, organizational-data and how-org-data-service-works; none states report enablement or a rollout default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The report assesses people attributes and manager relationships already used by Microsoft 365 experiences.
claims.quote: Your organizational data describes the people at your organization, what they do, where they sit, and who they report to. Microsoft 365 apps use that data to answer questions about people and teams.

claims.where: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not state whether this report lists named individuals.
claims.quote: Searched: "Organizational Data Service" "data quality" named users report permissions switch; "Organizational Data Service" "data quality" "read-only" "individual". Read data-quality-metrics and get-started; neither specifies named-person drill-down.

claims.claim: The getting-started page names Microsoft 365 Global Administrator as a role for signing in to the service.
claims.quote: First, sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center with an account that has the required administrative permissions (Microsoft 365 Global Administrator or Organizational Data Source Administrator).

claims.claim: The getting-started page names Organizational Data Source Administrator as a role for signing in to the service.
claims.quote: First, sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center with an account that has the required administrative permissions (Microsoft 365 Global Administrator or Organizational Data Source Administrator).

claims.where: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not reconcile the roadmap's report-access roles with the getting-started page's service sign-in roles.
claims.quote: Searched: "data quality report" "People Administrator" "AI Administrator" Microsoft 365 access location. Read roadmap record, get-started and organizational-data; they do not explain how the report-role and service sign-in lists relate.

claims.claim: The metrics documentation describes no automatic fix performed by the report.
claims.quote: Searched: "Organizational Data Service" "data quality" automatic remediation unique values segmentation. Read data-quality-metrics and organizational-data; no automatic report remediation is described, and metrics directs corrections to source owners.

claims.where: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft Entra ID takes precedence over Organizational Data Service for overlapping profile attributes by default.
claims.quote: By default, Microsoft Entra ID takes precedence over Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service.

claims.where: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Confirming a fix requires a refreshed assessment after corrected data flows through the source.
claims.quote: Confirming how many people a specific fix reconnects, or that a health label has changed, takes a refreshed assessment after the corrected data flows through the source.

claims.claim: Organizational Data Service licensing requirements vary according to the consuming Microsoft 365 or Viva app.

claims.claim: The service entry point in Microsoft 365 admin center is Settings > Viva > Data management > Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service.

On the left, under Settings, select Viva.
Under Data management, select Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service.

claims.claim: No API equivalent of this admin-center entry point or API/export for the data quality report is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft Graph" "organizational" "data quality report" API export; "Organizational Data Service" Microsoft Graph API admin center access report quality. Read get-started, metrics and Graph reports excerpts; no matching operation or report export appears.

claims.claim: The location of the report within Organizational Data Service is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "data quality report" "People Administrator" "AI Administrator" Microsoft 365 access location. Read get-started, data-quality-metrics and organizational-data; the service entry is documented but no route inside it to this report is given.

claims.claim: The reviewed pages do not document a report-specific on/off switch or access-restriction setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365" "data quality report" "enable" "default"; "Organizational Data Service" "data quality" named users report permissions switch. Read get-started, organizational-data and data-quality-metrics; no report-specific switch or access setting is given.

claims.claim: The report is read-only, changes nothing and cannot itself change people data.
claims.quote: Searched: "Organizational Data Service" "data quality" "read-only" "individual". Read data-quality-metrics and organizational-data; corrections generally belong in the authoritative source, but neither establishes an exclusively read-only report.
claims.fix: In the summary replace 'It is read-only and aimed at admins' with 'It is aimed at admins'. Replace the final Governance controls sentence with 'Corrections generally belong in the authoritative source that supplies the attribute.' In the risk rationale replace 'and, on the page Microsoft documents, changes nothing' with 'and Learn directs corrections to the authoritative source'. The narrower wording is supported by https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/org-data-service/manage/data-quality-metrics.

claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to check profile source precedence has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Check profile source precedence if a corrected value does not appear'. The sole table row is 'Entry point to Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service in the admin centre'.
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout bullet beginning 'Check profile source precedence if a corrected value does not appear'. The supported factual explanation can remain under Change & support.
